key_insight: EndoCoT endogenizes Chain-of-Thought (CoT) inside diffusion models so the multimodal LLM provides iterative, evolving reasoning guidance during generation rather than a single static encoding.
problem_solved: Addresses two bottlenecks in MLLM+diffusion pipelines: (1) shallow, single-step text encoding that fails to trigger CoT reasoning, and (2) invariant guidance across diffusion steps that cannot adapt to intermediate visual-linguistic states.
method: Embed an internal CoT loop into the diffusion sampling process so the MLLM produces multi-step reasoning updates that condition subsequent denoising steps.
Introduce a lightweight interface (adapter/prompts) between the diffusion latent states and the MLLM to enable iterative querying and conditional refinement without full model re-run.
Train with consistency and alignment objectives that encourage coherent, stepwise explanations and stable guidance across diffusion iterations, allowing scalable application to larger MLLMs.
impact: Enables more accurate and interpretable multimodal reasoning for complex tasks (e.g., spatial planning, compositional instructions) by turning static text guidance into a dynamic, self-refining signal—improving generation quality and trustworthiness for practitioners.

paper_title: EndoCoT: Scaling Endogenous Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Xuanlang Dai, Yujie Zhou, Long Xing, Jiazi Bu, Xilin Wei
